method: Manual domain and delivery-gate triage from the canonical section and requirement text. This assigns ownership and evidence boundaries; it does not claim implementation or acceptance.

ranges.reason: Cloud runtime, permission paths, and connector budgets require read-only vendor adapters.
restrictions: No cloud account or runtime sensor has been tested.

ranges.reason: Detection lifecycle, correlation compatibility, evidence mapping, and calibrated triage belong to the detection plane.
restrictions: No Sigma backend or purple-team lab acceptance exists.

ranges.reason: Attacker evidence, attribution boundaries, forensics, reporting, and evidence-first response belong to investigations.
restrictions: No active OSINT scan, honeypot, external report, or hack-back action is authorized.

ranges.reason: Detection content, schemas, audit readiness, and regression corpora form the detection engineering layer.
restrictions: Third-party rule licensing and backend compatibility need review.

ranges.reason: Forensic and endpoint analyzers require controlled adapters and acquisition profiles.
restrictions: No live memory, disk, endpoint, Linux, or macOS acquisition was run.

ranges.reason: NDR telemetry and sensor coverage are CyberGuard evidence inputs; network operations remain external.
restrictions: No packet capture, active scan, inline IPS, or sensor deployment was run.

ranges.reason: CVE enrichment, risk ranking, scanning governance, SBOM, and VEX form vulnerability management.
restrictions: No scanner result or remediation is verified.

ranges.reason: AD, cloud identity, and service identity evidence require least-privilege connectors.
restrictions: No AD, Entra, AWS, Azure, GCP, or Kubernetes account was connected.

ranges.reason: Threat intelligence and malware analysis require provenance, sandbox isolation, and licensing controls.
restrictions: No malware sample execution or external feed is enabled.

ranges.reason: Containment and isolation require typed actions, approval, impact checks, verification, and rollback.
restrictions: Current actions affect local metadata only; no endpoint or network containment.

ranges.reason: Enterprise product governance and repository controls are platform responsibilities.
restrictions: No enterprise deployment or production certification exists.

ranges.reason: Algorithm selection and cryptographic primitives are platform architecture concerns.
restrictions: Only approved library primitives may be used; no custom cryptography claim.

ranges.reason: TLS, PKI, and certificate lifecycle require deployment-specific integration.
restrictions: The current loopback preview is not a TLS deployment.

ranges.reason: Post-quantum readiness is a migration and inventory program.
restrictions: No post-quantum interoperability or performance test exists.

ranges.reason: Keys and secrets require dedicated vault and lifecycle integration.
restrictions: No enterprise vault or HSM is connected.

ranges.reason: Network encryption posture is security evidence; operational network changes remain NCC-owned.
restrictions: No device configuration write is implemented.

ranges.reason: Cloud key inventory and policy require provider-specific read-only connectors.
restrictions: No cloud KMS account is connected.

ranges.reason: Windows device identity and encryption evidence belong to the endpoint adapter.
restrictions: Only synthetic Windows event fixtures are Unit Tested.

ranges.reason: Signing and supply-chain controls belong to DevSecOps release gates.

ranges.reason: Cryptographic visibility and anomaly evidence feed detection and investigations.
restrictions: No live cryptographic telemetry source is connected.

ranges.reason: Product verification before prototyping is an architecture and release responsibility.
restrictions: Current status remains engineering preview.

ranges.reason: Configuration audit and hardening require applicability checks and staged rollout.
restrictions: Read-only evidence first; no hardening change executed.

ranges.reason: Policy-as-code decisions and dry runs belong to the approval gateway.
restrictions: No cloud or firewall policy execution is implemented.

ranges.reason: Linux and container runtime security requires kernel and admission-controller compatibility tests.
restrictions: No Linux or Kubernetes lab has been tested.

ranges.reason: Database audit evidence requires vendor-specific adapters and privacy limits.
restrictions: No database connector or credential is configured.

ranges.reason: Passive wireless and firmware evidence inform security; device operations remain integration-bound.

ranges.reason: Application security, SBOM, repository policy, and scanner ownership belong to DevSecOps.
restrictions: No DAST, SBOM monitor, or repository enforcement is active.

ranges.reason: Sensitive-data discovery and AI context controls require local classifiers and access governance.
